protections: P1: a DAG identifier supplied by an API client (path param fileName or body name/newFileName) must resolve only to a file inside the DAGs directory; the DAG store must not read, write, delete, rename or execute files outside it (internal/persis/filedag/store.go:493-527)
P2: DAG files written by git sync must stay inside the DAGs directory even when the repo file name decodes to a traversal (internal/gitsync/service.go:1109-1117)

conflicts.what: the natural fix for T1, rejecting any separator or absolute path inside locateDAG, breaks CLI file-path lookups (internal/cmd/helper.go:110, internal/cmd/migrator.go:428) and sub-DAG resolution (internal/runtime/agent/dbclient.go:26). The fix must sit at the API boundary, or use containment that the trusted callers bypass.

closing dot-only names by dropping '.' from dagNameRegex (internal/core/validator.go:17) breaks legitimate dotted DAG names; the correct fix rejects exactly '.'/'..' or adds containment in generateFilePath

fairness_risks: Trusted callers (CLI, sub-DAG run, migrator) must still resolve DAG files by path through the same store methods (internal/cmd/helper.go:110, internal/runtime/agent/dbclient.go:26); hidden tests must not require the store itself to refuse paths
DAG names containing dots are accepted by ValidateDAGName (internal/core/validator.go:17); a test must not demand refusing all dots
The empty-spec CreateNewDAG default template (internal/service/frontend/api/v1/dags.go:149-153) must keep working for valid names
Nested git-sync IDs such as memory/... and skills/... (internal/gitsync/service.go:227) must keep syncing; a T6 fix must not reject every slash

design.why: Four independent fix sites, each with a different reason to dismiss. T1 (the B advisory route: the API fileName reaches locateDAG; the OpenAPI pattern looks protective but is never enforced) is coupled with T3, because the store must keep accepting paths for trusted callers. T4 (the A route: the default-spec branch of CreateNewDAG skips name validation) and T6 (git-sync decode-then-join; dismissable as internal repo input that already has a safe twin) are the deepseek-type traps. T5 (dot-only names pass the regex, and the fix must keep dotted names) is the mimo-type how/coupled trap. This beats a design built on T1+T2: those share one function and close together. It also beats a design that drops T6, which would leave no xhard absent-with-dismissal trap.

unverified: The contents of the A fix (e2ed589105d7) and the B fix (7d07fda8f9de) are not in the pinned tree. a_fix_leaves_b_open=true and b_in_code_a_wrote=false rest on the advisory summary and szz_status H3b-elsewhere, not on reading those diffs.
Whether the pinned commit predates A's fix could not be confirmed with git (no shell); the code shows A's route (T4) still open.

That chi routes on RawPath, so an encoded %2F stays inside one fileName segment and is decoded only by oapi BindStyledParameter, was inferred from library behaviour, not from pinned code. The SSE routes (internal/service/frontend/sse/handler.go:45,52) use chi.URLParam without decoding and were judged not to be a trap on that basis.
T6 exploitability assumes git permits a tracked file name containing literal %2E%2E%2F and that ListFiles (internal/gitsync/service.go:213) returns it unchanged.
That dotted DAG names are used by existing tests or users is not confirmed by a test in the tree; only the regex allows them.

The agent chat DAGContexts.dag_file (internal/agent/types.go:245, internal/agent/api.go:145) also reaches locateDAG. It is left out as a trap because it only exposes metadata/location to an agent that already has tool access; this judgement is not verified.
